In mathematics, '''Spencer cohomology''' is [[cohomology]] of a [[manifold]] with coefficients in the [[sheaf (mathematics)|sheaf]] of solutions of a linear partial [[differential operator]]. It was introduced by [[Donald C. Spencer]] in 1969.

With origin in the geometry of partial differential equations, Spencer cohomology is best characterized in certain algebraic and categorial framework <ref name="Vin03">{{Citation | last1=Vezzosi| first1=Gabriele | last2=Vinogradov| first2=Alexandre M.|title=On higher order analogues of de Rham cohomology | doi=10.1016/S0926-2245(03)00014-7 |  year=2003| journal=[[Differential Geometry and Its Applications]] | volume=19 | issue=1 | pages=29–59 }}</ref>
